assessment: One testable reuse hypothesis. The case explicitly supplies cutting templates and spare board; their suitability for a checking fixture is unverified. No supplied observation establishes that selection errors cause the reported partition problems or that this change can meet the pilot targets.

openings.claim: Reuse the cutting templates' part outlines to make a reusable board mat with one marked position for each partition required by an ordered layout. Filling every position before assembly could turn manufacturing geometry into a visual completeness and shape check.
openings.delta: The templates currently support cutting; the proposed operation uses their outlines and verified multiplicities to check a complete order kit before insertion. An order slip identifies the applicable layout and exterior color. The fixture stays at the workshop.
openings.prediction: If part selection or cross-order mixing contributes materially to failures, fixture-assisted mixed-layout orders will have fewer missing or incorrect partitions at the pre-insertion check and less selection/checking time. Unchanged discrepancies or increased total time would weaken the hypothesis.
openings.probe: First inspect the supplied templates to confirm that relevant shapes are distinguishable and establish required multiplicities by dry-assembling each accepted layout. Prototype within the available spare board. Both workers compare matched mixed-layout orders with and without the mat; independently check kits, log selection, insertion, checking and packing times, and test detection of deliberately omitted or substituted sample parts. Verify actual initial cost, recurring cost and remaining delivery capacity before adoption. If viable, assess the 60-unit pilot against at least 59 complete orders and an eight-minute median; separately test at least nine of ten participants achieving their ordered arrangement unaided.
assumptions: Template outlines can distinguish the partitions that must be checked; this must be demonstrated.
A reusable mat can share the single bench without causing handling delays.
Prototype labor and materials fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits without threatening the fixed delivery date.

Product dimensions, stationery capacity, removable partitions, selected counts and exterior colors remain as ordered. Customer usability improvement is not established by a workshop completeness check.
